chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Khālid, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Samāʿah, who said:
I asked him about the hand, and he said: “Half of the diyah; and regarding the ear, half of the diyah, if he cuts it off from its root.”

key_terms.أَصْلِهَا: its root or base, meaning complete severance from the point of origin
key_terms.الدِّيَةِ: financial compensation due for bodily injury
key_terms.الْأُذُنِ: the ear, as an organ for which a fixed compensation is assigned
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, as a bodily limb subject to legal compensation
key_terms.قَطَعَهَا: he cut it off, referring to severing the organ
key_terms.نِصْفُ: half, indicating half of the full prescribed compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the diyah for cutting off a hand or an ear in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning bodily injury compensation. It states that the compensation for a hand is half of the diyah, and likewise for the ear when it is severed from its root.
